stem: While maintaining a sterile field, how should the nurse treat the outer 1-inch border of the field?

options.A: As contaminated; sterile items should be kept away from this border
options.B: As the preferred area for placing sterile instruments
options.C: As sterile only when the drape remains dry
options.D: As sterile once the nurse has donned sterile gloves

rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills identifies any part of a sterile field within 1 inch of the edge as contaminated. Sterile supplies should therefore be kept away from that border. Dryness or the nurse's use of sterile gloves does not convert the 1-inch edge into a sterile area. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Maintain sterile technique by recognizing the outer 1-inch border of a sterile field as contaminated.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_locator: Chapter 4, Sterile Fields / establishing and maintaining a sterile field: areas considered contaminated include any part of the field within 1 inch from the edge
source_claim_supported: The area within 1 inch of the edge of a sterile field is considered contaminated and should not be used for sterile items.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: maintain aseptic/sterile technique and reduce infection risk during nursing procedures
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — sterile-field maintenance
correction_summary: Preserved the clinically correct 1-inch border rule, replaced trivial distractors with realistic misconceptions about dryness and sterile gloves, and anchored the rule to an exact NCBI Nursing Skills sterile-field locator.
audit_findings: A directly matches the source. B uses the contaminated edge for sterile instruments; C and D incorrectly suggest conditions that restore sterility to the border. The item has one clear best answer, no unsupported precision beyond the directly sourced 1-inch rule, and direct infection-prevention relevance.
